report.executive_summary: Autonomous threat hunt completed. Multiple ATT&CK techniques confirmed.

findings.title: Brute Force Attack - Password Guessing Against Administrator Account
findings.description: 15 failed logon attempts (Event ID 4625) detected over 4 minutes (02:30:03 to 02:34:27) from source IP 192.168.1.105 targeting the CORP\Administrator account via network logon type (LogonType=3). All attempts failed with "Unknown user name or bad password" error reason. Pattern indicates systematic password guessing attack. Attack occurred between 02:30:03 and 02:34:27 on 2024-06-15, representing a concentrated brute force effort with multiple connection attempts from varying source ports.
evidence: All with reason: Unknown user name or bad password

findings.title: Successful Credential Compromise - Administrator Account Breach
findings.description: One successful network logon (Event ID 4624) for CORP\Administrator detected at 2024-06-15T02:36:44 from IP 192.168.1.105. This login occurred immediately after the brute force attempts (6 minutes later), indicating successful credential compromise. The attacker appears to have obtained valid Administrator credentials, either from a dictionary attack or leaked credentials. This successful login marks the transition from exploitation to post-compromise activity.
evidence: Occurs 6 minutes after last failed logon attempt

findings.title: PowerShell Command Execution - Malicious Post-Compromise Activity
findings.description: Multiple suspicious PowerShell commands executed by CORP\Administrator following successful logon, starting at 2024-06-15T02:42:02. Commands include: (1) Atomic Red Team framework import at 02:42:42, (2) System discovery commands (hostname, systeminfo, whoami, ipconfig, net user) executed at 02:42:44-02:46:13, (3) LSASS process enumeration at 02:46:20, (4) Windows Defender disablement via Set-MpPreference at 02:44:54 and 02:55:58. Pattern indicates attacker profiling system and disabling security controls following account compromise.

findings.title: Credential Dumping - LSASS Memory Extraction
findings.description: No description provided

findings.title: Credential Dumping - LSASS Memory Extraction
findings.description: Two complementary indicators of LSASS credential dumping attack: (1) Sysmon Process Access event (ID 10) at 2024-06-15T02:49:11 showing powershell.exe accessing lsass.exe with GrantedAccess 0x1010, (2) Direct process dump via procdump.exe at 02:49:27 with command "procdump.exe -ma lsass.exe lsass.dmp", executed from cmd.exe in Administrator context. Additionally, PowerShell command at 02:46:20 specifically enumerated LSASS process. This coordinated activity indicates attacker extracting memory credentials for lateral movement preparation.
evidence: Sysmon Process Access: powershell.exe accessing lsass.exe at 02:49:11 with GrantedAccess 0x1010
Parent process cmd.exe executed by Administrator

findings.title: Lateral Movement via SMB - Reusing Compromised Credentials
findings.description: Attacker performed lateral movement to adjacent systems using compromised Administrator credentials. Evidence includes: (1) net use command at 2024-06-15T03:01:45 targeting \\192.168.1.110\C$ with explicit Administrator credentials and password (Lab123!), (2) Two SMB network connections to 192.168.1.115:445 at 03:01:37 and 192.168.1.110:445 at 03:03:47. Both connections establish SMB shares (port 445) on target systems, indicating pivot attempt to adjacent infrastructure using the dumped/known credentials.
evidence: Credentials in cleartext in command line: Lab123!

findings.title: Persistence via Scheduled Task - Hidden PowerShell Execution
findings.description: Attacker created a persistent scheduled task at 2024-06-15T02:53:15 masquerading as Windows Update functionality. Event ID 4698 shows task creation named "\\Microsoft\\Windows\\WindowsUpdate\\UpdateCheck" by Administrator. Task content executes obfuscated PowerShell: "powershell.exe -NoP -W Hidden -c IEX(Ne..." with -NoProfile and -WindowStyle Hidden flags to evade detection. This provides persistence mechanism for remote code execution at scheduled intervals.
evidence: Scheduled task creation Event ID 4698 at 02:53:15
NoProfile flag to skip profile loading

findings.title: Defense Evasion - Windows Defender Disablement via Registry and PowerShell
findings.description: Attacker disabled Windows Defender protections through multiple methods: (1) PowerShell Set-MpPreference commands at 02:44:54 and 02:55:58 setting DisableRealtimeMonitoring and DisableBehaviorMonitoring to true, (2) Registry modification (Event ID 13) at 02:56:28 setting HKLM\\SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\DisableAntiSpyware, (3) Registry persistence key created at 03:06:20 in HKLM\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\WindowsUpdate pointing to C:\\Users\\Administrator\\App... This coordinated defense evasion allows malicious activity to execute undetected.

findings.title: System Discovery and Reconnaissance - Post-Compromise Profiling
findings.description: Immediately following credential compromise, attacker executed systematic system discovery commands via PowerShell to profile the compromised system: (1) hostname at 02:42:44, (2) systeminfo at 02:44:40, (3) whoami /all at 02:45:22, (4) ipconfig /all at 02:45:26, (5) net user at 02:46:13. All commands executed under CORP\\Administrator context via PowerShell parent process. This reconnaissance activity indicates attacker profiling system configuration, OS version, network interfaces, and user accounts prior to lateral movement, consistent with standard post-compromise reconnaissance procedures.
evidence: net user command at 02:46:13 (Sysmon Event ID 1)

findings.title: Registry Persistence - Run Key Modification
findings.description: Attacker created registry persistence mechanism at 2024-06-15T03:06:20 (Event ID 13) by modifying HKLM\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\WindowsUpdate key via reg.exe. Registry modification points to suspicious path C:\\Users\\Administrator\\App..., which likely contains malware payload to execute at system startup. This provides automatic code execution on system restart, complementing the scheduled task persistence mechanism.
evidence: Registry Run key for persistent code execution
